Given that $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{5}{8},$ the value of $x$ is
question.worked_solution:
The cosine of an angle is equal to the adjacent divided by the hypotenuse (C-A-H).

Relative to the angle $\theta ,$ the length of the adjacent side is $\frac{7}{4}x+29,$ and the length of the hypotenuse is $7x+17.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}} \\ \frac{5}{8} & =\frac{(\frac{7}{4}x+29)}{7x+17} \\ 5(7x+17) & =8(\frac{7}{4}x+29) \\ 35x+85 & =14x+232 \\ 21x & =147 \\ x & =7.\end{aligned}
$$
